Appearance:
 Shri Deependra Singh Raghuwanshi - Advocate for the app  Shri Dilip Awasthi -Govt. Advocate for the respondents/
 ORDER

This Miscellaneous Second Appeal has been filed under Section 76 (1) of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 against the order dated 02.09.2024 passed by Appellate Tribunal/8th District Judge,
Gwalior in RCA No. 189/2024 as well as order dated 14.5.2024 passed by Adjudicating Officer,
Gwalior in Case No. Q/Food Safety/98/2020.
2.
By order dated 14.5.2024, the Adjudicating Officer had imposed a penalty of Rs. 1,00,000/- under Section 51 and Rs. 10,000/- under Section 55.

Being aggrieved by the said order, the appellant preferred an appeal, which has been partially allowed, and the penalty imposed under Section 51 was reduced to Rs. 75,000/- and penalty imposed under section 55 was reduced to Rs. 5,000/- and now the total penalty of Rs. 80,000/- has been imposed.
3. Challenging the orders passed by the Courts/authority below, it is submitted by counsel for the appellant that the case was decided in utter violation of principle of natural justice.
The Examination-in-Chief of Ravi Kumar Shivhare NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:30123 2 MSA-18-2024 was recorded on 22-06-2022.

sentences.text: Thereafter, the case continued up to 26.12.2023 for examination of the departmental witnesses and on 26-12-2023, the following order sheet was recorded:-

FSO       
 PO   .         
   "
 4.
On 12-01-2024, the right of the appellant to departmental witness was closed.
However, the presence of any of the departmental witness was not recorded in the order dated 12-01-2024, and the case was fixed for final arguments.
The case was never fixed for recording of defence evidence of the appellants and ultimately, the final order was passed.

5. It is submitted that since no opportunity to cross-examine the departmental witness was extended to the appellant, therefore, evidence of the departmental witness which was not tested by any of the accused, by cross- examining him, cannot be looked into, and further, the valuable right of the appellant to lead defense witness was also not extended.
6. Per contra, the appeal is vehemently opposed by the counsel for the State.

However, after going through the order sheets, it was fairly conceded that the Examination-in-Chief of FSO was recorded on 22-06-2022, and thereafter, the case was adjourned because the adjudicating officer was busy in election duties.
7. Considered the submissions made by counsel for the parties.
8.

The order dated 22-06-2022 recorded by Additional District Magistrate/Adjudicating Officer is as under:-
  FSO   "           
 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:30123  3            
    ''
Sanchalak/Firm Kai Paan Product Pvt. ... vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79220337/
2 9.

From the aforesaid order sheet, it is clear that sentence "      
    " was inserted in the order sheet at a later stage in a different handwriting.

10. Be that whatever it may be.
11.

But in the same order sheet, it is also mentioned that since the Presiding Officer was busy in election duty, therefore the case was adjourned for further proceedings and in the subsequent order sheets, the case was then fixed for cross- examination of FSO.

On 26.12.2023, the presence of FSO Shri Ravi Shivare is recorded, but it was mentioned by the Reader of the Additional District Magistrate/Adjudicating Officer, that since the Presiding Officer is busy in other government works, therefore the case was adjourned for cross-examination, and it was fixed for 12-01-2024.
On 12-01-2024, the right of the appellant to cross- examine the FSO was closed, because the counsel for the appellant was not present.

However,
in the said order sheet, even the presence of FSO was not mentioned, therefore, it is clear that although the witness of the department was not present, but still the right of the appellant to cross-examine the witness was closed.
After closing the right of the appellant to cross-examine the departmental witness, the case was never fixed for recording of defense evidence.
By order dated 12-01-2024, the appellant was not proceeded ex-parte, but merely his right to cross-examine the witness was closed.

Under that circumstances, the Additional District Magistrate/ Adjudicating Officer should not have fixed the case directly for final arguments but should have fixed the case for recording of defense evidence.

Under these circumstances, this court is of the considered opinion that the procedure which was adopted by the Adjudicating Officer is unknown to the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:30123 4 MSA-18-2024 principle of natural justice and thus, it is vitiated.
Unfortunately, this fact had escaped from the notice of the Appellate Court also.
12. Since the order dated 14-5-2024 was passed by the Adjudicating Officer in utter violation of principle of natural justice, therefore, it cannot be upheld.
The orders dated 02.09.2024 and 14.5.2024 are hereby set aside.

Matter is remanded back to the Adjudicating Officer to decide the matter afresh after giving an opportunity to cross-examine the departmental witness Shri Ravi Shivhare as well as after extending an opportunity to the appellant to lead defense evidence.
13. The parties are directed to appear before the Adjudicating Officer on 17.12.2025.
14. With aforesaid observations, this Miscellaneous Second Appeal is allowed.
